To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derive new fixed-point methods for the blind separation and extraction of complex-valued signals from mixtures and that these algorithms perform well for small data-sets, as compared to existing approaches.

the fixed-point algorithms for complex ICA proposed in this paper are the best available methods for extracting multiple complex-valued sources from arbitrary mixtures of independent and noncircular, non-Gaussian signals.

(i) the separability properties of complex-valued, independent, and noncircularly-symmetric signal mixtures are more restrictive than those of the real-valued case, (ii) the kurtosis-based FastICA algorithm of real-valued ICA can be generalized to complex-valued mixures by using the complex kurtosis function, and (iii) the resulting fixed-point algorithms have fast convergence properties and are easy to use, and perform well in data-starved environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental question in signal processing: How can we separate a linear mixture of independent, non-Gaussian source signal mixtures?
the blind source separation (BSS) of arbitrary complex-valued non-Gaussian signal mixtures.
the problem of separating an observed mixture of signals into their constituent parts, without prior information about either the mixing or signal-generating processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed algorithm has the potential to outperform the best of the existing complex ICA algorithms in the case of a limited data record length, and it performs at least as well as the existing complex Ica algorithms when there is a large data record length.
our algorithms perform better than existing complex ICA algorithms, and are as good as the best of them, and are also very fast, easy to implement, and have very good convergence properties.
the proposed algorithms provide a significant step toward the solution of the complex blind source separation problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have derived a family of new algorithms for the blind complex ICA problem that can be applied to both real and complex signal mixtures and that are guaranteed to converge to the true solution under certain conditions.
the proposed algorithms are simple, efficient, and accurate in extracting complex-valued non-Gaussian source mixtures.
we have extended the FastICA algorithm to complex-valued signal separation problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FastICA algorithm is the natural starting point for the development of new fixed-point ICA methods for complex-valued signal separation.

the FastICA algorithm is not only a simple, fast, and reliable technique for the blind separation and feature extraction of real-valued data, but also a powerful tool for the blind separation or feature extraction of complex-valued data.
, in contrast to existing methods, the proposed algorithms can be applied directly to the complex-valued mixture without requiring the computation of a complex-to-real transform.
